criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure and headings are clear and an executive summary is present, but figures/tables lack numbering/titles, references are bare URLs and do not match in-text citations (e.g. [49]-[74] missing), Wikipedia is used, and grammar slips occur. Adequate low.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite
STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Kourou latitude is given as 45.05°N; Guiana Space Centre is about 5.2°N, so launch-site geometry discussion is wrong.
SSO inclination for 600 km is stated as 87.79°; correct value is about 97.8° retrograde. The graph indicates ~97.8°, so text/table are inconsistent and the defined orbit is not sun-synchronous.
Initial RAAN 27.33° is said to indicate launch facility; RAAN at epoch depends on launch time/date, not simply site.
Average contact duration stated as almost 20 min; table mean 580.786 s ≈ 9.7 min (max 12.8 min).
Claim descending path is constantly sunlit is unsupported; SSO normally has eclipses unless a dawn-dusk local-time orbit is specified.
No GSD/swath calculation; text says low resolution 'also desirable' where likely undesirable, undermining altitude rationale.
No link budget/data rate or ground-station capability analysis to show image data can be downlinked.
Drag-sail EOL chosen without deorbit lifetime/ballistic coefficient calculation or debris-mitigation compliance demonstration.
Text says only orbital manoeuvre occurs at EOL but then selects passive drag sail and says no thrusters; does not clearly state no operational manoeuvres.
Uses Wikipedia '2021 in spaceflight' and tables with citations [49]-[74] absent from reference list; not acceptable source.
No STK/PIGI software files included with report/appendix; only screenshots.

overall: Mission concept is appropriate and report is structured, but credibility is reduced by a wrong SSO inclination, incorrect Kourou latitude, overstated contact duration, missing data-link/swath analysis, missing STK files, and weak referencing.

feedback.summary: You present a clear, well-motivated reef-monitoring mission with a justified single-satellite concept and structured coverage of launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL, supported by STK screenshots. Credibility is reduced by the incorrect SSO inclination (87.79° vs ~97.8°), wrong Kourou latitude, overstated contact duration, missing link/swath calculations and STK files, and weak referencing. Addressing these will lift the report from Adequate toward Accomplished.
next_steps: Correct the orbital geometry: recompute the 600 km SSO inclination (~97.8° retrograde), fix Kourou's latitude (~5.2°N), and re-run STK so text, table and figure agree. Add a GSD/swath calculation to justify the 600 km altitude and clarify why low resolution is undesirable.

Strengthen quantitative evidence: reconcile the mean contact duration (~9.7 min, not almost 20 min), add a link budget/data-rate and ground-station capability analysis, and support the drag-sail EOL with deorbit-lifetime/ballistic-coefficient and debris-mitigation compliance calculations.

Improve evidence and referencing: include STK/PIGI files in an appendix, number and caption all figures/tables, replace the Wikipedia source, ensure citations [49]–[74] appear in the reference list, and explicitly define the operator and customers in the Introduction.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the mission need and single-satellite rationale with references. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify the operator and customers (not just implicit Australian facilities, UTAS and scientists), add detailed user/operations discussion, and use quality literature rather than bare URLs. Keep the strong rationale.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL with STK screenshots. Next level requires correcting the SSO inclination (~97.8°, not 87.79°), Kourou latitude (~5.2°N) and contact duration (~9.7 min mean); adding GSD/swath and link-budget calculations; including STK files; and supporting drag-sail EOL with deorbit-lifetime and compliance evidence.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion restates launch, orbit and ground-station choices. To reach Accomplished, include key quantitative outcomes (altitude, inclination, contact statistics, mission lifetime), state the EOL approach, and avoid overclaiming a fully described configuration. Tie conclusions directly to evidence in the main body.
criteria.C4: Structure, headings and executive summary are clear. Next level requires numbered/captioned figures and tables, consistent formatting, and a reference list matching all in-text citations (including [49]–[74]); replace Wikipedia with credible sources and proofread grammar. This will make the report professional and easy to follow.
